searchText: Hey all, does anyone use the `step` parameter in the `beacon_blocks_by_range` RPC method? Hey <@498009160982724610> , yeap we do Are you using it to interleave blocks from multiple peers? We use as part of our initial sync routine to distribute requested blocks across peers Yeap How do you handle a peer sending you an invalid block or an empty slot? if its a skip slot its easy to handle, as you can infer it when processing all the received blocks in one go. If a peer cant respond to our request, we redistribute it to our remaining peers We dont have any logic currently to ban/score peers for sending us invalid blocks Also, if you set the start slot to 0 and count to 100.. and skip slot is 2 for example.. and there are 50 skip slots, do you expect blocks over slot 100 to be returned? Yep, so to clarify.. consider 2 peers with interleved blocks. You get 50 blocks and every second one comes from a different peer. When you process them, you have a system of identifying which peer has sent the wrong block and remove it from sync? In the case of skip slots, we expect peers not to send us any blocks in that case. So we expect the slot to still be 100. We dont have anyway to identify if a peer did send us a bad block So we aggregate all our interleaved blocks And then process them ok cool. So the RPC response is always in the range `[start_slot, start_slot+count)` correct? I'm asking because we currently only use step=1 and I should add support to what you guys expect and perhaps make the spec a lil more explicit Ah no Actually it would be ``` [Start_slot, start_slot + count *step] ``` Ah yep, my bad. And skip-slots don't effect this range? and the last block there is non-inclusive right? The last block is inclusive Is the spec non-inclusive ? So if start_slot = 1 and count =100 and step=1.. you would expect 101 blocks to be returned? Nope skip slots dont affect this range Would the first slot be inclusive ? If not we might defer there Yeah. I take the first slot and inclusive and the last as exclusive Ah k I think we are on the same page then The count will be the number of blocks returned So 100 should be correct Ok, cool thanks. Will conform 🙂 Great 😀

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Hey all, does anyone use the `step` parameter in the `beacon_blocks_by_range` RPC method?

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Are you using it to interleave blocks from multiple peers?

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: We use as part of our initial sync routine to distribute requested blocks across peers

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Yeap

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: How do you handle a peer sending you an invalid block or an empty slot?

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: if its a skip slot its easy to handle, as you can infer it when processing all the received blocks in one go. If a peer cant respond to our request, we redistribute it to our remaining peers

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: We dont have any logic currently to ban/score peers for sending us invalid blocks

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Also, if you set the start slot to 0 and count to 100.. and skip slot is 2 for example.. and there are 50 skip slots, do you expect blocks over slot 100 to be returned?

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Yep, so to clarify.. consider 2 peers with interleved blocks. You get 50 blocks and every second one comes from a different peer. When you process them, you have a system of identifying which peer has sent the wrong block and remove it from sync?

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content:
In the case of skip slots, we expect peers not to send us any blocks in that case. So we expect the slot to still be 100. 

We dont have anyway to identify if a peer did send us a bad block

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: So we aggregate all our interleaved blocks

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: And then process them

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: ok cool. So the RPC response is always in the range `[start_slot, start_slot+count)` correct?

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: I'm asking because we currently only use step=1 and I should add support to what you guys expect and perhaps make the spec a lil more explicit

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Ah no

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content:
Actually it would be  
```
[Start_slot, start_slot + count *step]
```

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Ah yep, my bad. And skip-slots don't effect this range? and the last block there is non-inclusive right?

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: The last block is inclusive

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Is the spec non-inclusive ?

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: So if start_slot = 1 and count =100 and step=1.. you would expect 101 blocks to be returned?

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Nope skip slots dont affect this range

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Would the first slot be inclusive ? If not we might defer there

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Yeah. I take the first slot and inclusive and the last as exclusive

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Ah k I think we are on the same page then

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: The count will be the number of blocks returned

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: So 100 should be correct

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Ok, cool thanks. Will conform 🙂

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Great 😀
